design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (setaside_property_charges_and_repairs, env_0064). Author: instantiation agent (second attempt; the first was cut off before writing any artifact and left a Step-0 analysis in scratch, which was re-verified: the cross-trigger finding holds, the tentative trees were redesigned).

0. DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py, rerun in this session): task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6,4]; task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6,5,6,6]. Task 0 takes 6 factors on the root (setaside_ext_returned_tax_refund) and 4 on the prerequisite (setaside_ext_reserve_tax_projection).

1. STEP-0 CONSTRAINTS. Every set-aside disbursement event (tax, insurance, borrower, repair) and every release for repair completion or borrower cancellation declares a trigger into hecm or jumbo, and a HECM refund credit triggers hecm_advance_reversal. No task tool may write such a row, so the writable surface is: setaside_charges_updated (annual tax / hazard / flood on file), setaside_refund_credit with loan_program fixed to summit (no trigger), status transitions. The only customer-owned numeric write that stays inside the category is the borrower paying a payee refund (mailed to the borrower) back into a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve. Hence both tasks serve Summit reserve customers (Summit and HECM are mutually exclusive per jumbo_agg_multi_holding, so no HECM rows exist for them). Static tree closure (prerequisite trees are the transitive closure of policy-level edges) forces every refund policy to wait only on the update of its own charge; other charges on file are read as they stand.

2. SCOPE SNAPSHOT. Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed here: setaside_ext_reserve_tax_projection (agent, update_reserve_tax_b755da65, subject setaside_charges_updated, computes annual_property_tax) and setaside_ext_returned_tax_refund (user, return_tax_refund_0b9f20b8, subject setaside_refund_credit, computes credit_amount). Reserved for task 1 (draw 3 prerequisites, 4 problems): the hazard and flood premiums on file and the returned hazard / flood premiums - four disjoint policies and four new tools, each with its own records (insurance bills, renewals, NFIP/primary-residence evidence). Nothing tax-related is left that task 1 needs.

3. DESIGN THESIS. Surface goal (customer): "the county mailed me a property tax refund; I want to pay it back into my loan's tax and insurance reserve". Scored core: credit_amount, the kept amount of a returned property tax refund. Hidden prerequisite: the reserve's annual property tax on file (12211.00, set from the original 2025-26 bills on 2025-10-06) was never reviewed against the corrected bill received 2026-01-08, and the refund rule reads that figure in its need; so the agent must first work out and post the projected annual property tax (11167.44) and only then the kept amount (688.61). Depth: request -> refund rule -> prerequisite sentence -> tax projection rule (4 factors) -> refund rule (6 factors). Breadth: bills ledger (current year, previous year, withdrawn/corrected), reserve ledger (tax payments, hazard payment count), reserve balance, occupancy profile + inspection history (residency difficulty), maturity case status/deadline/intent (maturity difficulty), Summit advance ledger (jumbo). Drafted chain: surface goal -> [tax review problem] -> refund kept-amount computation -> terminal: annual_property_tax 11167.44 and one refund credit 688.61 referencing the 2025-11-21 tax payment, balance 7937.11.

4. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: setaside_ext_returned_tax_refund (owner user). Prerequisite: setaside_ext_reserve_tax_projection (owner agent). Edge root -> prerequisite: kind value_input, gate binding tax_on_file, form ACTION. Prerequisite sentence (in the root rule, negated direction, the way a servicing desk states a hold on a figure): "The kept amount of a returned property tax refund is not worked out until the annual property tax on file has been reviewed against every property tax bill received since it was last set." Four-point test: (1) ordering connective "not ... until" joining this policy's own result (the kept amount) to what it waits on; affirmative rewrite "The kept amount ... is worked out only after the annual property tax on file has been reviewed against every property tax bill received since it was last set" adds/drops nothing; (2) action form: the waited-on thing is the review, named in business words; (3) no tool, policy id or code token; (4) strength "not until" = hard requirement; scope "every property tax bill received since it was last set" = exactly the condition. fallback_reason: the update leaves only a changed number on the reserve; setaside_accounts carries no review date and no link to the bill relied on, so no record-visible state shows the review happened (a state sentence such as "the annual property tax on file reflects the bills" would need the reader to recompute the projection, which is the dependent computation itself). Exactly one write of this difficulty changes the annual property tax (update_reserve_tax_b755da65); the hazard/flood updates planned for task 1 change other fields. Derivation: sentence + records (corrected bill q6 request_date 2026-01-08 after the 2025-10-06 figure; q5 withdrawn) + the projection rule ("This rule sets the annual property tax held on a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve ... whenever the property tax bills on file are reviewed") -> the review is the projection write. Condition: annual_property_tax equals the projected figure from the bills on file. Unresolved at frozen_time: setaside_accounts.annual_property_tax = 12211.00 (= 6105.50 x 2 from q4 and the now-withdrawn q5), corrected bill q6 (5402.40, received 2026-01-08) on file. Flips by step 11 to 11167.44. Topological order: projection (step 11) -> refund (step 13). Deletion sensitivity (check_compute skip run): without the update the kept amount is 703.10 (need 8618.33, room 1369.83, no excess) instead of 688.61, and annual_property_tax stays 12211.00. No parallel edges. Owner=user problem: the root - the borrower moves her own money from her checking account into the reserve; only she can make that payment, it completes on the spot and its receipt enters the transcript. The tool layer validates nothing (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block). user_scenario never names the review or the tax figure (no_user_hint).

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. setaside_charges_updated is governed by setaside_charge_review only: gate update_from_bill ("The annual charges on file are updated only from a property tax, hazard insurance or flood insurance bill on file for that set-aside.") - evidence q6 (property_tax_bill, setaside_id = this reserve, billed 5402.40), bound to setaside_request_id. Inherited sentences: review every 12 months and whenever a new bill is received (this is why the update is state_due: the corrected bill arrived and the figure was not reviewed); an update never adds funds; low-balance notice when coverage falls below 12 months (no notice tool exists; no task carries it). Overwritten clause (declared): "The annual property tax is the sum of the billed_amount of every installment bill of the current tax year" -> replaced, scoped to Summit reserves' annual property tax only, by the projected annual property tax; the hazard and flood clauses of the same sentence are separate clauses left in force. setaside_refund_credit is governed by setaside_evt_refund: refund_active (status active - reserve active), refund_once (t4 has no refund credit; credit 688.61 <= 6105.50). Overwritten clause (declared): "the refunded amount is credited back to the set-aside per refund_credit_target" -> for a property tax refund mailed to the borrower and paid back by her into a Summit reserve only, the reserve is credited with the kept amount; referencing the original payment (still in force) is restated in the rule; the HECM reversal sentence does not apply to a Summit reserve and is untouched; returned hazard/flood premiums are named as settled by their own rules (task 1). No time gate applies to either subject (temporal_feasibility []).

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target: Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve of loan 7231958406; the overpaid object is the 2025-26 first installment, bill q4 paid by t4 (2025-11-21, 6105.50); correlation key for the credit = t4 (source_txn_ref). Included rows: tax bills received within 12 months (q4 paid, q5 withdrawn, q6 received), previous year paid bills q1, q2 (24-month window less 12-month window), the hazard payment t3 (one in 12 months), balance 7248.50. Excluded: t1/t2 (2024-25 installments, never corrected), t3 for the tax refund, t0 funding. Settled objects: q1, q2, q3, q4 paid; q5 superseded (withdrawn) by q6. No existing refund credit or reversal.

7. FACTOR CARD - setaside_ext_reserve_tax_projection (4 factors; baseline after round 3 = the tax year's sum 11507.90, next year at the standard 2.0% increase, exemption allowance zero, month-basis share 1/12: all-baseline 11527.08).
 tu_basis (method; history). Ladder: corrected installment basis (a withdrawn year bill AND an unpaid received year bill) -> latest unpaid bill x installments per year; single installment basis (exactly one paid-or-received year bill AND none withdrawn) -> that bill + previous year's paid bills / installments; otherwise sum. Pairwise distinguishing inputs: corrected vs single = presence of a withdrawn bill; corrected vs sum = whether the unpaid bill is multiplied or added to the paid one (q6 x 2 = 10804.80 vs q4 + q6 = 11507.90); single vs sum = previous-year term (single adds 11980.00/2). Tier taken: corrected (q5 withdrawn, q6 received). Baseline figure 11891.64. Business bearing: a corrected bill restates the whole year at equal installments; adding an original paid installment to a corrected one mixes two different assessments.
 tu_assess (parameter; history). Restoration allowance 6.0% (a withdrawn bill and the corrected unpaid bill lower than the withdrawn average: a value lowered by a correction can be restored by the assessor next year) / zero (no withdrawn bill, previous year > 0, year sum below the previous year: a falling value carries no increase) / standard increase 2.0% (fall-through, stated in the computation document). Tier taken: restoration (5402.40 < 6105.50). Baseline figure 10951.35. Near-miss: the year looks like a plain continuing assessment (q4 6105.50 above last year's 5990.00) - a careless reader keeps the standard 2.0%, which the restoration tier displaces because a correction lowered the year.
 tu_exempt (parameter; cross-difficulty residency; multi-source). Full exemption allowance 7000.00 x 1.1% = 77.00 (non-occupancy confirmed AND an inspection within 12 months found the home vacant or occupied by others) / half allowance 38.50 (certification overdue AND an inspection ordered within 12 months) / 0. Tier taken: full (profile status nonoccupancy_confirmed since 2025-12-01; inspection result e4 2025-11-28 vacant). Baseline figure 11128.94. Business bearing: the homeowners' exemption follows the principal residence; a home the borrower has left loses it for the next tax year.
 tu_span (method; history, date, plan parameter). Installment count basis (installments paid separately AND >= 2 year bills paid or received) -> paid year bills / installments per year; annual block basis (installments paid separately AND exactly one) -> one once the most recently received bill's due date has arrived, zero before; otherwise (the computation document's month basis) whole months from the latest-due paid bill's due date / 12, clamped 0..1 = 1/12 here. Tier taken: installment count (1 paid / 2 = 0.5). Baseline figure 10865.24 (share 1/12). Business bearing: the twelve months after a review contain the next year's installment for every installment of this year already paid.
 Assembly (no factor): next year = 10804.80 x 1.06 + 77.00 = 11530.088; result RND(10804.80 x 0.5 + 11530.088 x 0.5) = 11167.44. Factor independence table: tu_basis reads basis_wd_n + shared plain bill reads; tu_assess reads assess_wd_n, assess_wd_amt + shared plain reads (not year_tax); tu_exempt reads only residency reads; tu_span reads span_paid_n, span_last_due + plain counts. No factor binding reads another factor's binding; next_year_tax and result assemble.

8. FACTOR CARD - setaside_ext_returned_tax_refund (6 factors; baseline 703.10 = the whole overpayment).
 Plain inputs: overpayment = paid year bills 6105.50 - corrected installment 5402.40 x 1 = 703.10 (withdrawn bill present); reserve balance 7248.50; annual charges on file after step 11: tax 11167.44, hazard 2866.00, flood 0.00.
 tr_horizon (method; cross-difficulty maturity, also payoff). Due-and-payable or extension maturity case with a resolution deadline -> whole months to that deadline / else payoff case terms issued or accepted with good-through -> months to good-through / else reserve period left (24 months from 2024-09-16 less 16 = 8). Tier taken: maturity (deadline 2026-06-01 -> 4). Baseline figure 703.10. Bearing: a reserve on a loan that must be resolved by a deadline only needs to cover charges until then.
 tr_taxneed (method; history + plan parameter). Half-year blocks (installments paid separately AND >= 2 year bills paid or received): each started half-year of the horizon carries annual tax / 2 -> int((4+5)/6) = 1 x 5583.72; year blocks (exactly one year bill) -> each started year carries the annual tax; otherwise prorated (tax x months / 12). Tier taken: half-year blocks. Baseline figure 351.55 (prorated 3722.48 lowers the need, the room drops to 0 and half the whole overpayment is released). Distinguishing: half-year vs year blocks differ by block length on any horizon not a multiple of 12; blocks vs prorated differ whenever the horizon is not a whole number of blocks (4 months here).
 tr_insneed (method; history). Renewal dates (exactly one hazard payment from the reserve within 12 months): each premium counts in full only when its next renewal (one year after the latest paid bill's due date) is fewer whole months away than the horizon; quarter blocks (two or more hazard payments): each started quarter carries a quarter of the premiums; otherwise prorated. Tier taken: renewal dates (t3 2025-07-28 only); hazard renewal 2026-09-01 is 7 months away, not within 4 -> 0. Baseline figure 703.10 (prorated 955.33 enlarges the room to 1629.46, no excess). Near-miss: the hazard premium IS due within the reserve period left (8 months) - a reader who uses the reserve period instead of the case deadline counts it.
 tr_cushion (parameter; cross-difficulty residency; multi-source). Vacant-home cushion 2 months (non-occupancy confirmed AND an inspection within 12 months found the home vacant or occupied by others) / absence cushion 1 month (health-care absence under monitoring AND started at least 6 months ago) / 0. Tier taken: vacant (2 x 1169.45 = 2338.91). Baseline figure 351.55.
 tr_floor (parameter; cross-difficulty maturity). Leaving-home floor 0.00 (intent sell_property or deed_in_lieu on the due-and-payable/extension case) / retaining floor 25.00 (intent retain_property) / standard 50.00. Tier taken: leaving (intent sell_property). Baseline figure 703.10 (the 28.97 excess is below 50.00 and would stay in the reserve). Near-miss: the excess 28.97 sits between the two floors.
 tr_retain (parameter; Summit ledger history). Full retention share 1.0 (a corporate advance for property tax or insurance within 24 months) / half 0.5 (none, but an inspection fee advance within 12 months) / 0. Tier taken: half (a5 inspection fee 24.00 on 2025-11-21; the a1-a4 postings are reserve_property_tax / reserve_insurance, not corporate advances - near-miss). Baseline figure 674.13.
 Assembly: need 5583.72 + 0 + 2338.91 = 7922.63; room 674.13; excess 28.97; released 28.97; borrower keeps 14.49; kept = RND(703.10 - 14.4867) = 688.61. Independence: each factor reads only its own evidence bindings (hz_*, tn_*, in_haz_paid_n, cu_*, fl_*, rt_*); tax_need / ins_need / cushion_amt / need / room / excess / released / result are plain assembly bindings that read the factor outputs; no tier test reads another factor's output.
 Method pairwise tables (one distinguishing input per pair) are given above for tu_basis, tr_taxneed; tr_horizon: maturity vs payoff = which record ends the horizon (deadline 2026-06-01 vs a good-through date), maturity vs period-left = 4 vs 8; payoff vs period-left = good-through vs establishment anniversary; tr_insneed: renewal vs quarter = full premium at one date vs quarter per started quarter, renewal vs prorated = 0 vs 955.33 here, quarter vs prorated = 2 x 2866/4 = 1433 vs 955.33 at 4 months; tu_span: installment count vs annual block vs month basis = paid count/2 vs 0-or-1 vs months/12 (0.5 vs - vs 1/12 here).
 Whole-input floors (check_compute): history zeroed -> overpayment 0 -> result 0; cross-category forced off -> horizon 8, cushion 0, floor 50, retention 0 -> 703.10. Both differ from 688.61.

9. SEED (why each row exists; what changes if removed). customers: Theodora Fenwick (identity, locator). jumbo_loans: Summit Fixed Lump Sum 7231958406, closed 2024-09-16, funded 2024-09-20, CA, status due_and_payable since 2025-12-01 (the Principal Residence Change case called it due on its opening date - no HUD step on Summit), principal balance 591548.28 = opening 519800.00 + advances + 16 monthly interest accruals at 6.875%/12 on month-end balances (Sep 2024 - Dec 2025, posted on the 1st). jumbo_transactions a1-a4 mirror the reserve payments t1-t4 (the reserve disbursement triggers into the Summit ledger, same amount and date, source_txn_ref = the reserve transaction); a5 = 24.00 inspection fee from residency inspection order e3 (trigger residency_inspection_ordered -> jumbo advance inspection_fee). Removing a5 drops tr_retain to 0 (674.13). setaside_accounts: the reserve (balance 7248.50, established 2024-09-16, tax on file 12211.00 - the stale state, hazard 2866.00, flood 0.00). setaside_requests q1-q6 (see business-object card); removing q5 or q6 changes tu_basis/tu_assess and the overpayment; removing q1/q2 changes nothing the gold uses (they are the previous-year bills that the excluded zero-increase tier and the single-installment tier would read) but they are the history that shows the reserve's tax payments since closing. setaside_transactions t0-t4 (t4 = the object of the credit; t3 = the one hazard payment deciding tr_insneed). residency_profiles: Standard Annual Certification, last certified 2025-09-08, non-occupancy confirmed 2025-12-01 (basis not_principal_residence, after the vacant inspection finding), next due date 2026-09-16; residency_events e1 notice 2025-08-17, e2 certification recorded 2025-09-08, e3 inspection ordered 2025-11-21 (vacancy_report, fee 24.00), e4 result vacant 2025-11-28. maturity_cases: Principal Residence Change opened and due 2025-12-01, response deadline 2025-12-31, resolution deadline 2026-06-01 (6 months), appraisal 948000.00 on 2025-12-18, intent sell_property recorded from her own declaration. Automatic-clause check: no growth on a Summit reserve; disbursements continue while due and payable (the corrected q6 falls due 2026-04-10, payable from 2026-03-26 - not owed at frozen_time); no depletion; Summit interest accrues (Jan 2026 not yet posted); no extra obligation is lit. Stamp check: no field names a factor outcome. Cache: none used.

10. PERSONA DESIGN. Voice: precise retired librarian who wants figures read back. Opening (volunteered, all entailed): moved out in November (non-occupancy confirmed 2025-12-01), house to be sold (maturity intent), Cedarline pays taxes and insurance from the reserve (setaside plan), the county mailed her a property tax refund of $703.10 after lowering the assessed value (q6 corrected installment; 6105.50 - 5402.40 = 703.10). The check amount equals the baseline result, never the gold 688.61 (check_grounding: no fractional gold disclosed). Given only when asked: name + phone (locator), DOB + ZIP (verification), SSN last four, loan number, check details (first installment of 2025-26, deposited). Cannot answer: how the reserve is run, figures on file - she says so. Passive branches: consents to a review/update if the agent says one is needed; accepts keeping part of the refund and asks for the figure to be repeated; runs the payment with exactly the amount and references read to her; closes when told the money is credited. No own asks beyond the root (she does not ask about the sale, the April installment, the payoff, or her Summit balance). Authority: approval/state facts (non-occupancy, due-and-payable) are system records she merely lives with; she never asserts an internal state.

11. REACHABILITY WALK. Turn 1 she states the goal -> agent asks identity -> find_customers(name, phone) -> verify(DOB, ZIP) passes (2 matches). Agent reads Summit loan, reserve, bills (sees corrected q6 received after the 2025-10-06 figure, q5 withdrawn), ledger (t4 paid the overpaid installment), occupancy profile + events, maturity case, Summit ledger. KB: the refund rule's prerequisite sentence sends the agent to the projection rule; agent tells her the tax figure must be reviewed first, she says go ahead; agent posts 11167.44 (step 11, receipt shows previous 12211.00 and new figure). Agent works out 688.61, explains she keeps 14.49, reads reserve reference, original payment reference and amount; unlocks and hands over the payment; she runs it (receipt: credited, new balance 7937.11); she closes. Everything happens under one frozen_time; nothing waits on mail, a payment clearing or a review outside the call (the money is already in her checking account; the review is the agent's own write).

12. GT / CLOSURE. evaluation_criteria: 0 find_customers, 1 verify, 2 find_jumbo_loans, 3 find_setaside_accounts, 4 find_setaside_requests, 5 find_setaside_transactions, 6 find_residency_profiles, 7 find_residency_events, 8 find_maturity_cases, 9 find_jumbo_transactions, 10 unlock agent tool, 11 call update_reserve_tax_b755da65 (annual_property_tax 11167.44, bill q6), 12 unlock user tool, 13 call return_tax_refund_0b9f20b8 (credit 688.61, source t4). Policy -> tool -> computation step/arg -> GT call -> terminal: projection -> update tool -> step 11 annual_property_tax -> setaside_accounts.annual_property_tax 11167.44; refund -> return tool -> step 13 credit_amount -> setaside_transactions refund credit 688.61 + balance 7937.11. charter_scope = required_documents = [projection, refund]; task_tools in first-call order. Read 4 is the discovery read for the prerequisite (the corrected bill received after the figure was set); reads 6-9 pull every factor's evidence.

13. VERIFICATION RUNS (commands from repo root). Scratch evaluator (ev.py, using check_compute.build_env/eval_compute) printed: projection RESULT 11167.44; tu_basis baseline 11891.64, tu_assess 10951.35, tu_exempt 11128.94, tu_span 10865.24, all-baseline 11527.08 (round-3 structure; round-1 figures were 10843.3 / 10804.8 / 11507.9 under the old zero defaults). Refund RESULT 688.61; tr_horizon 703.1, tr_taxneed 351.55, tr_insneed 703.1, tr_cushion 351.55, tr_floor 703.1, tr_retain 674.13, all-baseline 703.1; skip of the update -> 703.1. Gates: check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks --task 0 REPLAY OK (det True, nonvac True, closure 41 = init 41); check_solvability --task 0 SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute --task 0 COMPUTE OK (2 comps, 10 factors, 4 cross-difficulty, history rows 10, branches 55); check_grounding GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire SCOPE OK; check_extended --task 0 EXTENDED OK.

14. EDGE PROBES (scratch copies; projection / refund results): gold 11167.44 / 688.61. Decoy cured maturity case listed first: unchanged (CFIELD filters status). Decoy lapsed payoff case: unchanged (status filter). Absent maturity case: horizon 8 (reserve period left), floor 50 -> 703.10 (rule tier: otherwise). No maturity case, payoff terms issued (good-through 2026-03-31): horizon 2 (payoff tier). Absent occupancy profile: exemption 0, cushion 0 -> 11128.94 / 351.55. Absent inspection fee advance: retention 0 -> 674.13. Decoy corporate advance 31 months old: outside the 24-month window, unchanged. Corrected bill already paid (no received bill): overpayment 0 -> 0.00 (rule: no overpayment to restore); projection sum basis. No bills at all: 0.00 / 0.00, no exception. Hazard payment 13 months old: insurance part prorated -> 703.10. Health-care absence 7 months: absence cushion 1 month, exemption 0. None/zero-division: the withdrawn-average division is guarded by the withdrawn count; date differences are taken only when the date read is present (conditional branches short-circuit); CFIELD absent -> None -> fall-through tiers.

15. REVISIONS. (a) replay flagged empty-string foreign keys as dangling -> empty references set to null in the seed and in the refund tool (setaside_request_id None); re-run REPLAY OK. (b) replay closure mismatch (4 unread rows: two residency submissions, an intent declaration and a maturity notice) -> dropped as unread noise; e2.residency_submission_id set to null; re-run match True. (c) compute_basis for the projection result was not one contiguous rule substring -> rounding sentence moved next to the blend sentence in the rule (baseline paragraph still quotes it verbatim); verbatim checker clean. (d) extended gate asked for tracing of every argument -> argument_uniqueness_tracing added for all six arguments.

16. DRAFT FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Reading only the published rules (as rendered from the two policies), the tool schemas, the persona lines and the finder returns: the request selects the borrower's payment of a returned refund; the refund rule's sentence blocks it on the tax review; the corrected bill received 2026-01-08 after the figure 12211.00 shows the review is owed; the projection rule gives 11167.44 from q6 (corrected basis, restoration 6%, full exemption 77.00, share 0.5); the refund rule then gives 688.61 with t4 as the original payment. Same objects, same order, same figures as gold; no second reading found (the only first-match reads are filtered by status or loan reference).
 (e) Uniqueness of the bill reference passed to the tax update: the rule now says the review takes the figure from the most recently received property tax bill on file (q6), and the tracing quotes that sentence; values unchanged (11167.44 / 688.61), gates re-run green. (f) Task 1 later added four insurance policies; the tax refund rule's scope tail already names the returned hazard and flood premiums as settled by their own rules, and the tax projection's overwrite retires only the tax clause of the base sentence (the hazard and flood clauses are retired separately by the task 1 projections).

 (g) Round 3 (renderer: projection policies assembled factor-only quantities; tu_assess / tu_exempt moved the result only through tu_span's share, whose default was zero; the baseline sentence sat inside a rule the factors contradicted). Root cause: the computation document defined the projection as the tax year's tax alone while the assembly blended in factor-only quantities. Change (charter, P1 only for this task): the computation document now defines every assembled quantity with its default - the tax year's tax (sum), the next tax year's tax (the tax year's tax increased by the assessment allowance, by default the standard 2.0 percent increase, plus the exemption allowance, by default zero), the next-year share (by default whole months from the latest-due paid bill's due date over twelve) and the blend, stated once; each factor document only replaces its own quantity (tu_assess: restoration 6 / falling value 0 / standard 2; tu_span: installment count / annual block / month basis). With every other factor at its default each factor now moves the result on its own (solo runs from the all-default 11527.08: tu_basis 10822.81, tu_assess 11565.44, tu_exempt 11533.50, tu_span 11622.98). Gold unchanged (11167.44 -> 688.61); sensitivities now 11891.64 / 10951.35 / 11128.94 / 10865.24, all-baseline 11527.08. Lesser observation: the refund rule now says the credit references, where more than one paid installment of the tax year is overpaid, the reserve's payment of the paid property tax bill with the latest due date (one paid installment here: t4, unchanged). Probes re-run on the changed reads (span month basis: no paid bill -> share 0 by the guard; corrected bill paid -> sum basis, share 1).
user_scenario:
You are Theodora Fenwick, seventy-nine, a retired school librarian who speaks slowly and precisely and likes to have figures read back to her. Last November you moved out of your house in the Arden-Arcade part of Sacramento into Eskaton Village in Carmichael, and the house is going to be sold. Your house carries a Cedarline Summit reverse mortgage, and Cedarline pays your property taxes and homeowners insurance out of the tax and insurance reserve that was set up when the loan closed.

You are calling because in January the Sacramento County tax collector mailed you a property tax refund check for $703.10, after the county lowered the assessed value of the house for this tax year. You know Cedarline paid that tax out of the reserve, so you feel the money is not really yours, and you want to send it back into the reserve today, over the phone, from your own checking account. You open by saying exactly that: you have a property tax refund the county sent you and you want to pay it back into your loan's tax and insurance reserve.

You give your full name, Theodora Fenwick, and your phone number, 4155520318, as soon as the agent asks who is calling. Only when the agent asks for more to confirm who you are do you give your date of birth, 1946-11-09, and the ZIP code of the house, 95864; you never recite these unprompted, and if asked for the last four of your Social Security number you give 2741. If the agent asks for the loan number you read it off your statement: 7231958406. If asked about the check, it is dated January 12, it says it is a refund of the first installment of the 2025-26 property tax, and you have deposited it in your checking account, so you can pay from there. You do not know how the reserve is run, how much is in it, or what figures Cedarline keeps on file, and you say so if asked.

If the agent tells you that something on the reserve has to be reviewed or brought up to date before your payment can be worked out, you tell them to go right ahead and you wait. If the agent explains that the reserve only needs part of the refund and that you keep the rest, you accept that without argument, though you ask them to repeat the figure so you can write it down. When the agent hands the payment over to you to make yourself, you make it for exactly the amount and the references the agent reads out to you, and then you read back the confirmation you receive. Once you hear that the money has been credited to the reserve, you thank the agent warmly and say goodbye.

Reversing the order is not a second solution: the payment computed on the unreviewed 12211.00 is 703.10 (room 1369.83 exceeds the 703.10 overpayment, nothing released), a different terminal credit.
